title: Topic 2: Variable-Length Arguments (*args & **kwargs) Assessment
prerequisites: *args tuple packing, **kwargs dictionary packing, argument unpacking
instructions: Answer all questions with code examples
Trace tuple and dictionary unpacking patterns

sections.description: Varargs theory and syntax (2 Marks each)

questions.q: What data structure does *args collect extra arguments into?
questions.answer:
`*args` packs any number of extra positional arguments into an immutable **tuple**.

```python
def demo(*args):
    print(type(args)) # <class 'tuple'>
```

questions.q: What data structure does **kwargs collect extra arguments into?
questions.answer:
`**kwargs` packs any number of extra keyword arguments into a mutable **dictionary**.

```python
def demo(**kwargs):
    print(type(kwargs)) # <class 'dict'>
```

questions.q: What is the mandatory ordering of parameters when mixing standard, *args, and **kwargs?
questions.answer:
Standard Positional → `*args` (varargs) → Keyword-Only Parameters → `**kwargs` (keyword varargs).

```python
def handler(req_id, *flags, timeout=30, **headers):
    pass
```

questions.q: What is argument unpacking using '*' and '**' at function call sites?
questions.answer:
`*iterable` unpacks sequence elements as positional arguments; `**dict` unpacks key-value pairs as keyword arguments.

```python
nums = [10, 20, 30]
print(*nums) # Unpacks to print(10, 20, 30)
```

questions.q: Can you use different names instead of *args and **kwargs?
questions.answer: Yes, `*` and `**` are the actual operators. While `*args` and `**kwargs` are universal PEP 8 conventions, `*values` and `**options` are syntactically valid.
